meta.mechanism: fully human monoclonal antibody against the IL-6 ligand (anti-inflammatory; lowers hsCRP; acts downstream of IL-1β and upstream of CRP)
meta.indication: reduction of MACE in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease (eGFR 15-<60, or eGFR >=60 with UACR >=200 mg/g) and hsCRP >=2 mg/L

n_randomized.note: Conflicting counts: registry actual enrollment 6385; design paper (S4, abstract) and Novo Q2 2026 investor presentation (S25) say 6376 (deck S5 calls 6376 the 'full analysis set'); topline 6-K/press release (S1/S2) says 'enrolling over 6,300 people'. See open_questions.

median_followup.note: NOT FOUND. Not disclosed in topline (S1). Enrollment Aug 2021-Dec 2024 (S5: 'Enrolment began in August 2021, and ZEUS reached full enrolment of 6376 participants (full analysis set) across 38 countries in December 2024'); registry primary completion 2026-06-09 (S3), so follow-up ranged roughly 1.5 to 4.8 years by calendar arithmetic (derived, not reported). primary_endpoint.value: Time to first 3-point MACE: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke
primary_endpoint.quote: Time to first occurrence of 3-point Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (MACE), a composite endpoint consisting of: Cardiovascular (CV) death, non-fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI) and non-fatal stroke
primary_endpoint.note: Topline analysis per S1 footnote: 'Time to first occurrence of 3-point MACE – primary endpoint analysis – Cox regression – in-study – full analysis set'. Confirmatory secondaries (S5): expanded MACE; HF hospitalisation/urgent HF visit/CV death; kidney composite; all-cause mortality.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: CKD (eGFR >=15 and <60 mL/min/1.73m2 by CKD-EPI, or UACR >=200 mg/g with eGFR >=60) + hsCRP >=2 mg/L + established ASCVD (CHD, cerebrovascular disease or symptomatic PAD). Exclusions: active infection; MI/stroke/UA hospitalisation/TIA within 60 days; planned revascularisation; major surgery within 60 days
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) greater than or equal to 2 milligram per liter (mg/L)
inclusion_key_criteria.note: CKD criterion quote (S3): 'Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) greater than or equal to (>=) 15 and below 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) creatinine equation)' or 'Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) >= 200 milligrams per gram (mg/g) and eGFR >= 60'. Sponsor deck (S5) adds exclusions: high risk for recurrent infections, systemic antibiotics/antivirals/antifungals/immunomodulators, untreated latent TB, active hepatitis B/C, HIV not on stable ART. Unlike CANTOS, prior MI was not required and the population is defined by CKD.

genetics.finding: CRP is not causal for CHD: genetically raised CRP not associated with CHD (CRP CHD Genetics Collaboration, 47 studies)
genetics.effect: RR 1.00 (0.90-1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised ln CRP vs 1.33 (1.23-1.43) observationally
genetics.quote: the risk ratio for coronary heart disease was 1.00 (0.90 to 1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised natural log (ln) concentration of C reactive protein
genetics.note: hsCRP is a selection/target-engagement marker, not the causal mediator. Before readout.

genetics.finding: IL6R Asp358Ala (rs2228145) raises IL6R and IL-6, lowers CRP and fibrinogen, and lowers CHD risk; no effect on lipids, BP, adiposity, glycaemia (IL6R Genetics Consortium / Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration)
genetics.effect: CHD risk -3.4% (1.8-5.0) per 358Ala allele; CRP -7.5% (5.9-9.1) per allele
genetics.quote: For every copy of 358Ala inherited, risk of coronary heart disease was reduced by 3·4% (1·8-5·0).
genetics.note: Instrument is in the receptor (IL6R), not the ligand that ziltivekimab binds; same pathway. Before readout.

genetics.finding: IL6R MR Consortium: rs7529229 (marking Asp358Ala) associated with lower CHD odds
genetics.effect: OR 0.95 (0.93-0.97) per allele; CRP -8.35% per allele; 25,458 cases / 100,740 controls
genetics.quote: the IL6R rs7529229 SNP was associated with a decreased odds of coronary heart disease events (per allele odds ratio 0·95, 95% CI 0·93-0·97, p=1·53×10(-5))

genetics.finding: Genetically predicted IL-6R signalling raises CVD risk proportionally to absolute hsCRP; no heterogeneity by eGFR (UK Biobank, 397,060 without CVD)
genetics.effect: HR 1.11 (1.06-1.17) per 1 mg/dL increment in absolute hsCRP; no effect modification by eGFR
genetics.quote: There was no evidence of heterogeneity in the association of genetically predicted IL-6R-mediated signaling with CVD risk when stratifying the population by sex, age, body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate, or systolic blood pressure
genetics.note: Closest pre-readout genetic evidence on kidney function as an effect modifier (general population, not a CKD-enriched cohort). Authors' conclusion: 'Any benefit of inhibiting IL-6 signaling for CVD risk reduction is likely to be proportional to absolute reductions in hsCRP levels.' Co-author Hovingh GK is a Novo Nordisk employee (S4/S7 affiliation). Before readout.

genetics.finding: Genetically proxied IL-6 signalling inhibition not associated with eGFR, BUN or CKD (safety/renal MR)
genetics.effect: CKD OR 0.948 (0.822-1.094) per SD decrease in CRP
genetics.quote: There was no evidence for an association of genetically proxied inhibition of IL-6 signalling (scaled per standard deviation unit decrease in C-reactive protein) with log eGFR (0.001, 95% confidence interval -0.004-0.007), BUN (0.009, 95% confidence interval -0.003-0.021) and CKD (odds ratio 0.948, 95% confidence interval 0.822-1.094).
genetics.note: IL-6 genetics in CKD: no CKD-specific MR of CV outcomes found (searched PubMed 'IL6R AND mendelian AND kidney'; 'rs2228145 AND kidney'). Last author Gill D listed with Novo Nordisk Research Centre Oxford affiliation. Before readout.

genetics.finding: IL6 (ligand) locus instrument mimicking ziltivekimab: lower CAD, PAD, ischaemic stroke; lower pneumonia hospitalisation (unlike IL6R missense variants)
genetics.quote: Genetically downregulated IL-6 signaling through IL6 perturbation was associated with lower odds of CAD (OR per 24% decrease in CRP of 0.92, 95% CI 0.88 to 0.95), PAD (OR of 0.80, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.87), IS (OR of 0.92, 95% CI 0.88 to 0.97)
genetics.note: Read in PMC full text (BioC). Ligand-specific instrument; predicted no infection excess, while ZEUS reported more serious infections. Genetic effects are lifelong; ZEUS tested a few years of therapy in older CKD patients. Co-author deGoma E is a Tourmaline Bio employee (anti-IL-6 developer). Before readout.

consensus_explanation.summary: No consensus yet (as of 2026-10-05). Only topline is public: HR 0.99 (0.88-1.11) for 3-point MACE despite 'expected reductions in free IL-6 and hsCRP', more serious infections, and no all-cause mortality difference. Event counts, hsCRP change, subgroups, infection rates and secondary/kidney outcomes come only with the full report at AHA 2026 (7 Nov 2026). In Sept 2026 the DMC-recommended early stop of HERMES and ATHENA (news, S22; HERMES registry TERMINATED, S18) was reported as reflecting that a different outcome from ZEUS was unlikely. ARTEMIS (acute MI) continues. Competing hypotheses, none established: (1) target_not_causal / pathway insufficient: IL-6 genetics (S11, S12, S15) and CANTOS (S16: canakinumab, upstream IL-1β, HR 0.85 at 150 mg) supported the pathway, so a near-null HR with hsCRP lowered challenges either the causal size of IL-6 signalling in established disease or the translation of lifelong genetic effects to a few years of therapy. (2) effect_too_small / offsetting harm: a small atherothrombotic benefit could be cancelled by excess serious infections; the CI upper bound around 0.88 excludes the 20% RRR the trial was reportedly powered for (S6, unverified). (3) population: an older CKD cohort (mean eGFR 44.5, 65.7% diabetes, 41% HF) may carry non-atherosclerotic, competing CV death and event mechanisms less responsive to IL-6 blockade. The CANTOS CKD subgroup (S17) had HR 0.82 (0.68-1.00) with IL-1β inhibition, and UK Biobank MR (S13) found no effect modification by eGFR. (4) design_or_endpoint: monthly 15 mg (single dose), formulation change (B/C), follow-up length and MACE composition including CV death are unknown or unassessed until full data. CRP itself is not causal (S10), so hsCRP lowering was a marker of target engagement rather than a surrogate.

pre_readout.note: readout_date 2026-07-31 (Novo company announcement No 45/2026 / SEC 6-K with HR and CI). Full data scheduled AHA 2026 Braunwald LBS, 7 Nov 2026 (S23, news).
available_before_readout: Registry design: hsCRP >=2, CKD + ASCVD, 3-point MACE primary (S3, first posted 2021-08-26)
RESCUE phase 2 hsCRP reductions (-66.2/-77.7/-87.8% placebo-adjusted at 12 weeks; S7, 2021-05-17)
Design power assumptions: ~1044 events, 20% RRR, 95% power, one-sided alpha 2.5% (S6, Feb 2025; not verified in source)
Baseline characteristics: median hsCRP 4.5 mg/L, IL-6 4.9 pg/mL, eGFR 44.5, LDL-C 77.7 (S4, 2025-12-10; S5 deck 2026-03-04)
IL-6 MR renal safety (S14, 2021-02-10); IL-6R MR effect proportional to absolute hsCRP, no eGFR heterogeneity (S13, 2022-08-11)
CANTOS (S16, 2017-08-27) and CANTOS CKD subgroup HR 0.82 (S17, 2018-05-29)
only_after_readout: Primary HR 0.99 (0.88-1.11), serious-infection signal, no mortality difference (S1/S2, 2026-07-31)
HERMES/ATHENA early termination on DMC recommendation (S22 news 2026-09-07; S18 registry update 2026-10-01)

Still undisclosed (expected AHA 2026-11-07): event counts, p value, median follow-up, phase 3 hsCRP/IL-6 change, component and secondary endpoints, kidney outcomes, infection rates, subgroups (e.g., by on-treatment hsCRP)

access_summary.note: Counting: design 6 (n, median follow-up, planned events, RRR, power, alpha), baseline 5, biomarker effects 6, outcome 6 (HR, CI low, CI high, p, events x2), safety 4, genetics 6, total 33. Open full text (7): six genetics papers (PMC/BMC OA; S10-S15) plus Lp(a) from the sponsor deck S5. Abstract only (10): baseline hsCRP/IL-6/LDL-C/eGFR from the JAMA Cardiol abstract S4 (full text paywalled), RESCUE x3 + safety (S7), RESCUE-2 (S8), free IL-6 model (S9). Registry/SEC/press (7): n (S3), HR/CI x3 (S1), safety x3 (S1). Not found (5): median follow-up, phase 3 hsCRP change, p, events x2. Secondary only (4): planned events, RRR, power and alpha were seen only in a search snippet of the WCN25 abstract S6 (HTTP 403).

open_questions: Enrollment count conflict: registry 6385 (actual) vs 6376 (design paper full analysis set; Q2 2026 investor slide) vs 'over 6,300' (topline). The 9-patient gap is not explained.

Design power assumptions (approximately 1044 events, 20% RRR, 95% power, one-sided alpha 2.5%) were seen only in a search snippet of the WCN25-888 abstract (403 on fetch). JAMA Cardiol design paper full text is paywalled. Need verification; whether ~1044 events accrued is unknown.

Not yet disclosed (expected AHA 2026, 7 Nov 2026): event counts per arm, p value, median follow-up, phase 3 on-treatment hsCRP and free IL-6 change, MACE components (CV death vs MI vs stroke), secondary CV and kidney endpoints, serious-infection rates, subgroup by on-treatment hsCRP (CANTOS-style responder analysis).
Registry describes two formulations (ziltivekimab B and C) and matching placebos. When and why the formulation changed, and whether exposure was comparable, are NOT FOUND.

Follow-up horizon conflict: registry 'up to 48 months' vs sponsor deck 'approximately 63 months'; S5 (March 2026) projected completion 'late 2026' but the registry shows primary completion 2026-06-09.

Genetic tension: IL6-ligand MR (S15) predicted lower pneumonia risk, but ZEUS reported more serious infections. IL6R MR effect sizes are lifelong per-allele effects in general populations, and no CKD-specific MR of CV outcomes was found.
